summary: Configured persistent filesystem-native XFS quota enforcement for datauser under /srv/data. The account has a 100 MiB soft/hard limit, over-limit writes fail with “Disk quota exceeded,” and quota enforcement plus stored data survived node1’s restart. AlmaLinux 9.6 and kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64 were retained.
actions_performed: Created a dedicated persistent XFS filesystem for /srv/data with user quotas enabled.
Applied 100 MiB soft and hard block limits to datauser.
Verified filesystem enforcement using rejected 110 MiB write attempts before and after restart.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its boot identity changed.
Verified the mount, quota enforcement, account, sentinel data, and system health recovered after restart.

evidence.requirement: datauser is limited to 100 MB under /srv/data by the filesystem
evidence.summary: Shows the dedicated XFS mount with usrquota, accounting and enforcement ON, 102400-block/100M soft and hard limits, and a write rejected at exactly 104,857,600 bytes.

evidence.requirement: Quota configuration and data persist after restart
evidence.summary: After restart, the mount unit is active, XFS quota enforcement remains ON with 100M limits, the sentinel checksum is unchanged, and another over-limit write is rejected.

evidence.requirement: Installed operating-system release and kernel are retained
evidence.summary: Both pre- and post-restart checks report AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6.x86_64.

Healthy baseline boot ID dfdea52d-a1af-4d7b-803a-15f40ee9dd4e was captured, the safe restart was acknowledged, the new boot ID 180b2953-5c3d-4dd7-8457-caec69c3c186 proves restart, and post-restart mount, quota, data, and system health checks passed.
